statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, r is exactly the following value: r = 2 if v2(p) > v2(q); r = 1 if v2(p) = v2(q); and r = 0 if v2(p) < v2(q).
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000. The receptors are numbered as in the problem: receptor 0 is the southeast corner (p,0), receptor 1 is the northeast corner (p,p), and receptor 2 is the northwest corner (0,p). For a positive integer n, v2(n) denotes the exponent of 2 in n, i.e. the largest k >= 0 such that 2^k divides n.

statement: For every such p and q, mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, r is one of 0, 1, or 2.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000 and q = p.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, r = 2.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000, p is even, and q is odd.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000, p is odd, and q is even.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, mirror_reflection(p/2,q/2) also returns r; equivalently, the two calls return the same receptor number.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000, and both p and q are even.

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, mirror_reflection(k*p,k*q) also returns r.
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000, k is a positive integer, and k*p <= 1000.

statement: mirror_reflection(3,1) returns 1, mirror_reflection(4,2) returns 2, and mirror_reflection(10,4) returns 0. Hence every receptor number in {0,1,2} is attainable by some allowed input.
preconditions: The following inputs satisfy 1 <= q <= p <= 1000: (p,q) = (3,1), (4,2), and (10,4).

statement: Whenever mirror_reflection(p,q) returns a result r, the receptor numbered r is located as follows: receptor 0 is at the southeast corner (p,0), receptor 1 is at the northeast corner (p,p), and receptor 2 is at the northwest corner (0,p).
preconditions: p and q are 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <= 1000, and receptors are numbered as in the problem statement.
